newsitem.title: ITALY: Alitalia says 96 group loss 1.2 trln lire.
newsitem.headline: Alitalia says 96 group loss 1.2 trln lire.

text.p: Italy's debt-laden flag carrier Alitalia said on Friday it posted a consolidated group loss of 1.203 trillion lire after accounting for restructuring costs of 901 billion lire.

The figure, contained in a statement issued after a board meeting, compared with a consolidated group loss of 85.9 billion lire in 1995. Alitalia itself posted a loss of 1.217 trillion lire in 1996 against a 1995 profit of 1.3 billion lire.
The statement said sales revenue in 1996 was 7.814 trillion lire, up 3.3 percent on 1995. Net financial indebtedness at the end of 1996 fell to 2.343 trillion lire from 3.420 trillion at end-1995.
Total indebtedness fell to 3.831 trillion lire, down 829 billion, while net financial charges fell to 331 billion lire, down 85 billion from a year earlier.

Italy requested European Union permission last year for a capital injection worth some 3.3 trillion lire into Alitalia to prepare it for privatisation. Italy and the European Commission are still trying to iron out differences over the plan.

The 1996 results were the ninth straight year of losses for Alitalia, which agreed to a rescue package with unions last June after a long and bitter battle over plans to slash staff costs and boost productivity. Friday's statement said three trades union representatives had been co-opted to the board.
